  [Y2] guess: Those retransmissions are failed connection attempts (SYN retransmissions), not successful data retransmissions.
  [Y3] guess: No SYN-ACK/ACK reverse traffic is generated, consistent with TCP not establishing rather than only forward data loss.
  [Y4] guess: TCP does establish, but data or ACK loss prevents any payload from being delivered, so the retransmissions are data retransmissions.
  [Y5] guess: TCP completes its handshake before the measured window; afterward its data segments are tail-dropped by the persistently full FIFO queue, so no ACKs return, RTO backs off, and only a few data retransmissions occur.
  [Y6] guess: With l1.queue.length=1000, UDP still fills l1 and TCP data or ACKs remain lost, or the sender's known window stays zero, so tcp_goodput_bps stays 0.

  [Y8] guess: The RTT values are stale TCP RTT estimates from a handshake or early ACK before the measured window; a longer queue increases the forward queueing delay seen in that sample, and reverse ACK traffic is not reflected in the measured-window l1_util_back.

  [Y10] guess: TCP type makes no meaningful difference at queue length 1000 because UDP tail drops and RTO backoff dominate, so no other TCP type exceeds 5792 bps by more than 1%.
  [Y11] guess: TcpBic's binary increase may let more initial segments survive the UDP-filled FIFO, so it could exceed 5792 bps by more than 1%.
  [Y12] guess: A longer FIFO gives a TCP burst more chances to be enqueued and acknowledged, so q=1000 should be at least as good as shorter queues for Cubic.
  [Y13] guess: A shorter queue such as 250, 500, or 750 packets reduces queueing delay or loss enough to give more than 5850 bps for Cubic.
  [Y14] guess: NewReno's loss response or Vegas's delay-based backoff prevents a successful data burst through the UDP-filled FIFO, leaving them in retransmission/RTO backoff.

A guess that takes up an earlier one with a stated difference (another cause, another range, a reason why the earlier test was not fair) is not a repetition. This is not the researcher's first guess, and a later guess has to be the fruit of what was learned since the earlier ones. The records marked NEW are what it says it learned from. Say in your reasoning what they show that the earlier guesses did not have, and ask: would the researcher have made this same guess without them? If yes, the citation is for form only and the defect is not_from_what_was_learned.

On sender's side packets wait in one queue of the knob l1.queue.length packets; a packet that arrives when it is full is dropped. Flow udp is UDP from sender to receiver: packets of 1400 bytes at a constant rate (2 Gbps). Flow tcp is TCP from sender to receiver: it always has data to send; its congestion control is the knob tcp.type. A host with more than one link forwards packets. In each simulation the flows start within the first 10 ms, traffic runs for one second that is not measured, and then for duration seconds, over which the outputs are measured.
THE SETTINGS THE RESEARCHER MAY CHANGE: l1.queue.length (4 to 1000, default 100); tcp.type (TcpCubic, TcpNewReno, TcpLinuxReno, TcpBbr, TcpVegas, TcpBic, default TcpCubic)
TOLERANCE: two results that differ by less than 1 % count as equal.

  [Y1] guess: The FIFO queue is persistently full from UDP, so TCP's connection packets are dropped and TCP never establishes, delivering no payload.
  [Y2] guess: Those retransmissions are failed connection attempts (SYN retransmissions), not successful data retransmissions.
  [Y3] guess: No SYN-ACK/ACK reverse traffic is generated, consistent with TCP not establishing rather than only forward data loss.
  [Y4] guess: TCP does establish, but data or ACK loss prevents any payload from being delivered, so the retransmissions are data retransmissions.
  [Y5] guess: TCP completes its handshake before the measured window; afterward its data segments are tail-dropped by the persistently full FIFO queue, so no ACKs return, RTO backs off, and only a few data retransmissions occur.
  [Y6] guess: With l1.queue.length=1000, UDP still fills l1 and TCP data or ACKs remain lost, or the sender's known window stays zero, so tcp_goodput_bps stays 0.
  [Y7] guess: Almost all l1_drops are UDP drops, so a few TCP segments can be acknowledged and give small positive TCP goodput while the total drop count remains huge.
  [Y8] guess: The RTT values are stale TCP RTT estimates from a handshake or early ACK before the measured window; a longer queue increases the forward queueing delay seen in that sample, and reverse ACK traffic is not reflected in the measured-window l1_util_back.
  [Y9] guess: At queue length 1000, TCP goodput is limited by loss and RTO backoff, so congestion-control behavior such as loss response, pacing, and recovery can change the delivered TCP goodput.
  [Y10] guess: TCP type makes no meaningful difference at queue length 1000 because UDP tail drops and RTO backoff dominate, so no other TCP type exceeds 5792 bps by more than 1%.
  [Y11] guess: TcpBic's binary increase may let more initial segments survive the UDP-filled FIFO, so it could exceed 5792 bps by more than 1%.
  [Y12] guess: A longer FIFO gives a TCP burst more chances to be enqueued and acknowledged, so q=1000 should be at least as good as shorter queues for Cubic.
  [Y13] guess: A shorter queue such as 250, 500, or 750 packets reduces queueing delay or loss enough to give more than 5850 bps for Cubic.
  [Y14] guess: NewReno's loss response or Vegas's delay-based backoff prevents a successful data burst through the UDP-filled FIFO, leaving them in retransmission/RTO backoff.

On sender's side packets wait in one queue of the knob l1.queue.length packets; a packet that arrives when it is full is dropped. Flow udp is UDP from sender to receiver: packets of 1400 bytes at a constant rate (2 Gbps). Flow tcp is TCP from sender to receiver: it always has data to send; its congestion control is the knob tcp.type. A host with more than one link forwards packets. THE SYSTEM, in the brief's words: A network of 2 hosts: sender, receiver. Link l1 joins sender and receiver: it carries 1Gbps with a one-way delay of 50us. On sender's side packets wait in one queue of the knob l1.queue.length packets; a packet that arrives when it is full is dropped. Flow udp is UDP from sender to receiver: packets of 1400 bytes at a constant rate (2 Gbps). Flow tcp is TCP from sender to receiver: it always has data to send; its congestion control is the knob tcp.type. A host with more than one link forwards packets. In each simulation the flows start within the first 10 ms, traffic runs for one second that is not measured, and then for duration seconds, over which the outputs are measured.

THE SYSTEM, in the brief's words: A network of 2 hosts: sender, receiver. Link l1 joins sender and receiver: it carries 1Gbps with a one-way delay of 50us. On sender's side packets wait in one queue of the knob l1.queue.length packets; a packet that arrives when it is full is dropped. Flow udp is UDP from sender to receiver: packets of 1400 bytes at a constant rate (2 Gbps). Flow tcp is TCP from sender to receiver: it always has data to send; its congestion control is the knob tcp.type. A host with more than one link forwards packets. In each simulation the flows start within the first 10 ms, traffic runs for one second that is not measured, and then for duration seconds, over which the outputs are measured.
THE SETTINGS THE RESEARCHER MAY CHANGE: l1.queue.length (4 to 1000, default 100); tcp.type (TcpCubic, TcpNewReno, TcpLinuxReno, TcpBbr, TcpVegas, TcpBic, default TcpCubic)
TOLERANCE: two results that differ by less than 1 % count as equal.

THE RESULT the guess is about: The measured TCP goodputs are 1158 or 5792 bps, i.e. one or five 1448-byte segments over 10 s, and the drop/UDP-goodput differences track small TCP segment counts.
THE GUESS of why it came out so: The queue-length pattern and retransmission/drop counts are integer segment-accounting effects: queue length changes how many segments of a few TCP bursts are enqueued, delivered, or dropped, displacing UDP packets.
THE HYPOTHESIS H12: At l1.queue.length=4, TcpLinuxReno's tcp_goodput_bps is not more than 1% above TcpLinuxReno's tcp_goodput_bps at l1.queue.length=1000.

Flow udp is UDP from sender to receiver: packets of 1400 bytes at a constant rate (2 Gbps). Flow tcp is TCP from sender to receiver: it always has data to send; its congestion control is the knob tcp.type. A host with more than one link forwards packets. THE SYSTEM, in the brief's words: A network of 2 hosts: sender, receiver. Link l1 joins sender and receiver: it carries 1Gbps with a one-way delay of 50us. On sender's side packets wait in one queue of the knob l1.queue.length packets; a packet that arrives when it is full is dropped. Flow udp is UDP from sender to receiver: packets of 1400 bytes at a constant rate (2 Gbps). Flow tcp is TCP from sender to receiver: it always has data to send; its congestion control is the knob tcp.type. A host with more than one link forwards packets. In each simulation the flows start within the first 10 ms, traffic runs for one second that is not measured, and then for duration seconds, over which the outputs are measured.
